title: Syriac Catholic and Syro-Malankara Eucharistic book states

traditions.label: Syriac Catholic celebrant missal
traditions.scope: Syriac Catholic altar missal, anaphora selection and ordinary; excludes Maronite and Chaldean recensions.
traditions.coverage_note: Bounded 1843 → 1922 revision described by the primary source; medieval Catholic reception and later original revisions remain incomplete.

traditions.label: Syriac Catholic deacon and server books
traditions.scope: Complementary Eucharistic minister books; not successive whole altar missals.
traditions.coverage_note: Held 1881 Mosul book role corrected; the 1868/1905 auxiliary line remains uninspected.

traditions.label: Syro-Malankara Catholic
traditions.scope: Catholic source-language repertoire and original Eucharistic legislation; independent vernacular translation history deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: 1934 two-anaphora book documented from contemporary page image; 2007 rubrical act read; the 1934 original and later Taksa origins are still missing.

sources.title: Missale Syriacum juxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae Syrorum (Rome: Propaganda Fide, 1843), original book
sources.inspection: Complete 279-page provider PDF retained. Latin title/imprint PDF 10 and patriarchal attestation with Roman imprimaturs PDF 272 independently read by two researchers. The source passage title-and-patriarchal-attestation binds hash 4bc875a28f40dc1868619121a7a4e413f58b7093610d66ad35df79f4f6896132. The seven anaphora openings at printed 103, 119, 128, 138, 146, 155, 168/PDF 134, 150, 159, 169, 177, 186, 199 were independently read by two researchers; Presanctified opening printed 53/PDF 84 also inspected.
sources.limitations: No complete liturgical transcription or complete comparison with the 1922 prayer bodies. Printed pagination and provider PDF page numbering remain distinct.

sources.title: Missale iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Apostolicae Antiochenae Syrorum auctoritate recognitum (Sharfeh, 1922)
sources.inspection: Full provider PDF acquired. Direct page images read: Latin title PDF 6; Rahmani address/decree PDF 8–9 (printed 3–4); dissertation PDF 10–20 (printed 5–15), especially revision description PDF 17–20 (printed 12–15); native contents PDF 22–23; Syriac title PDF 339. Native contents PDF 23 reread independently on 2026-10-17 against the 1843 headings; seven labels verified.
sources.limitations: Complete bytes do not mean complete body collation. Syriac/Arabic prayer bodies not transcribed. Rahmani’s historical authorship and confessional judgments are editorial assertions, not independently verified textual identifications.

sources.title: Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani: patriarchal decree accompanying the revised Missal, 8 December 1922
sources.inspection: Direct images PDF 8–9 (printed 3–4): authority identified at opening; prescription and Beirut, 8 December 1922 dateline on PDF 9.
sources.limitations: Act is read in its printed book witness. Prescribed use is not empirical proof that every community adopted it.

sources.title: ULB Bonn catalogue: Missale iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Apostolicae Antiochenae Syrorum auctoritate recognitum

stages.label: Rome missal with seven named anaphoras
stages.scope: Original Catholic celebrant missal with directly checked title, patriarchal attestation and seven anaphora section openings.
stages.witness_label: Missale syriacum juxta ritum ecclesiae Antiochenae Syrorum, Rome: Typis S. Congregationis de Propaganda Fide, 1843
stages.summary: The seven named anaphoras are James, Peter, John Chrysostom, Xystus, Matthew the Shepherd, Basil and John Evangelist. Rahmani identifies shortened entrance prayers and a Presanctified compilation constructed from secret prayers of James as features of this 1843 edition.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1843 Roman missal and seven-title roster, plus a consignation-of-chalice rite.
Explicitly names the 1843 edition when rejecting three attributed anaphoras, restoring shortened entrance prayers and replacing its constructed Presanctified form.
Confirms exact Latin title, publisher and 1843 imprint.

evidence.locus: Latin title PDF 10; attestation and imprimaturs PDF 272
evidence.claim: Original 1843 Propaganda imprint and patriarchal attestation dated Aleppo, 31 August 1840, directly read.
Original headings establish the seven named anaphora sections; the Presanctified opening explicitly identifies the signing-of-the-chalice service.

stages.limitations: Original title, attestation and anaphora labels are checked; entrance-prayer restoration and the derivation of the Presanctified compilation remain the 1922 editor’s descriptions. Prayer bodies are not fully transcribed. Shared author labels do not establish textual identity or historical authorship.
stages.reception: Patriarch Ignazio Pietro Giarve attests on 31 August 1840 that the book contains the Syriac missal and rubrics used by Syriac patriarchs, archbishops, bishops and priests in churches and convents. Roman imprimaturs by Dominicus Buttaoni and Joseph Canali appear on the same page. These are the book’s historical attestations; they do not prove uniform later use in every diocese.

stages.label: Mosul deacon and server service book
stages.scope: Auxiliary Mass-service book: deacon/congregation parts with priest cues, seasonal and departed propers, and pontifical service. Distinct book role from the altar missal.
stages.witness_label: Ketābā de-tešmeštā de-qurābā be-kullkēn dīlējātā le-fut teksā de-ʿēdtā qaddīštā de-Surjājē; French title Service de la Messe selon le rit syrien avec les prières qui se disent pour les morts, Nouvelle édition, Mossoul: Imprimerie des Pères Dominicains, 1881
stages.summary: The ordinary begins with instructions to the deacon and prints deacon/congregation texts around abbreviated priest cues. The Arabic contents distinguish daily service, seasonal/departed propers and pontifical service. Ziadé places the 1868/1881 Mosul Service de la messe line under diaconicon.

evidence.claim: Title gives 1881 imprint; Arabic approval dated 8 September 1880 explicitly identifies Syriac Catholics.

evidence.locus: PDF 382 printed 7; PDF 375 printed 14; PDF 365–360 printed 24–29; contents PDF 5–13
evidence.claim: Ordinary supplies minister/congregation text and priest cues; contents show complementary service material.
Identifies Mosul 1868 Service de la messe privée and its 1881 new edition as an early diaconicon.

stages.limitations: A full priest anaphora repertoire is not established by this book. Approval in 1880 is separate from publication in 1881. No whole-missal successor or predecessor relationship to 1922 is inferred.
stages.reception: Arabic approbation expressly addresses Syriac Catholics of Mosul. Its role is auxiliary to celebrant books; the same Eucharistic rite does not make it a new whole-missal state.

stages.label: Rahmani’s revised altar missal
stages.scope: Revised Syriac Catholic celebrant book with selected anaphoras, ordinary/prayer changes, Presanctified rite, rubrics and Arabic parallel public prayers.
stages.witness_label: Missale iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Apostolicae Antiochenae Syrorum auctoritate recognitum; Ketābā de-taksā de-qūrrābā; Typis Patriarchalibus in Seminario Sciarfensi de Monte Libano, 1922
stages.summary: James is revised against older manuscripts and Greek; John Evangelist is followed by Twelve Apostles, Basil of Caesarea, Mark, Eustathius and Cyril of Jerusalem. The editor suppresses Peter/Xystus and rejects three 1843 attributions. He removes conclusions after individual James diptychs; replaces the fraction/consignation formula with “Panem coelestem frangimus”; restores entrance prayers and changes Holy Thursday/Holy Saturday and dismissal prayers. The Presanctified rite is replaced, and solemn-celebration rubrics and preparatory/concluding prayers are added. Arabic is printed beside appropriate Syriac public prayers.

evidence.claim: Title identifies edition; James correction and diptych-conclusion removal are explicitly described.
Lists retained/new selection and rejected titles; retains the later six-part diptych arrangement in Twelve Apostles rather than newly introducing it.
Describes fraction, feast/prayer, dismissal, Presanctified and other changes.
Describes Arabic parallel prayers, solemn rubrics, canon-derived admonitions and optional prayers before/after Mass.
Patriarch’s decree dated 8 December 1922 prescribes the edition for his patriarchate and wherever his rite is observed.

stages.limitations: These are primary-described changes, not independent before/after Syriac collation. The editor’s authorship/confessional diagnoses are not adopted as modern critical conclusions. His statement about no alteration to institution narrative/epiclesis is narrower than “no changes to anaphoras.” The six-section Twelve Apostles diptychs are an explicitly retained feature, not a new 1922 innovation. The James manuscript-reference footnote is malformed as printed and needs shelfmark disambiguation.
stages.reception: Issued by Syriac Catholic patriarch Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani. The decree makes this edition alone authentic within his stated jurisdiction/rite; it does not legislate for all West Syriac churches or prove universal actual adoption.

stages.label: Catholic Pampakuda two-anaphora missal
stages.scope: Source-language Catholic book identified by contemporary bibliography; bounded repertoire state.
stages.witness_label: Pampakuda Syro-Malankara missal, 1934 (historical bibliographic designation; exact native title not yet inspected)
stages.summary: Tisserant reports two anaphoras: Xystus and James in its short form. This identifies a different selected repertoire from the 1931 Pampakuda collection and from Rahmani’s 1922 selection, without proving which books furnished its text.

evidence.claim: Identifies the Pampakuda 1934 Syro-Malankara missal and names only Xystus and short James.

stages.limitations: Original title, approval, ordinary, anaphoras and Presanctified leaves remain unacquired. Composition dates, identity of short James and direct textual parentage are unestablished. No substantive 1931 → 1934 or 1922 → 1934 transition is established here.
stages.reception: Contemporary source explicitly distinguishes this Syro-Malankara Catholic book from earlier Pampakuda collections. Common West Syriac ancestry alone does not prove Catholic reception of every earlier text.

stages.label: Synodal Holy Qurbono concelebration directions
stages.scope: Original 2007 synodal prescription of three Eucharistic concelebration rubrics; distinct from an independently uninspected revised Taksa.
stages.witness_label: Fifth Ordinary Holy Episcopal Synod, 9–12 October 2007, Decisions 5.i–iii, published in Malankara Synodal Acts and Voice 3.2 (February 2008), page 40
stages.summary: The main celebrant says prayers before the Institution Narrative aloud; concelebrants pronounce the Institution Narrative and chant epiclesis in a low voice; they remain standing during intercessions (Thubden).

evidence.claim: Original synodal directions specify voice allocation and posture.
Same report announces a revised Taksa release but does not establish that these directions were already inserted in it.

stages.limitations: Earlier rubrics have not been identified, so this is an attested prescribed rubrical state with no fabricated before/after transition. The 2008 journal date is not the decision date. This original rule is in scope; independent English/Malayalam translation history remains deferred.
stages.reception: Directions of the Syro-Malankara Catholic synod. Published prescription does not by itself prove adoption rates or exact printing in the released Taksa.

transitions.summary: The original 1843 anaphora headings and 1922 contents establish a different seven-title selection.

changes.before: 1843 roster: James, Peter, John Chrysostom, Xystus, Matthew the Shepherd, Basil, John Evangelist.
changes.after: 1922 native roster: James, John Evangelist, Twelve Apostles, Basil of Caesarea, Mark, Eustathius and Cyril of Jerusalem.
changes.locus_after: 1922 native contents PDF 23; Latin explanation printed 13/PDF 18

evidence.claim: Directly read the seven original anaphora attributions.
Directly read the seven anaphora attributions in their printed order.
Directly read the seven original anaphora attributions.
Directly read the seven anaphora attributions in their printed order.
The editor expressly identifies rejected 1843 compositions and the revised selection.

transitions.limitations: This is a comparison of native repertoire labels, not complete anaphora texts. A shared Basil title does not identify the same composition: the 1922 editor expressly rejects the 1843 Basil attribution. No general manuscript ancestry follows.

transitions.summary: Rahmani’s edition reports restoration of entrance prayers shortened in 1843 and replacement of the 1843 James-based Presanctified compilation by a manuscript Basil-labelled rite.

changes.before: Some entrance propitiatory prayers were shortened in the 1843 edition.
changes.after: These prayers are restored in full in 1922.
changes.locus_before: 1843 entrance-prayer bodies not yet collated; named retrospectively in 1922 printed 14, paragraph Orationes propitiatorias introitus.

evidence.claim: Explicit 1843 → present edition restoration statement; individual prayer bodies not collated.

changes.before: The 1843 editor constructed the Presanctified rite by collecting secret prayers of the James liturgy.
changes.after: The 1922 book replaces that compilation with a manuscript-derived Presanctified liturgy bearing Basil’s name, for Lenten fast days.
changes.locus_before: 1843 Presanctified begins printed 53/PDF 84; its derivation from James is described in 1922 printed 14.
changes.locus_after: 1922 printed 14 / PDF 19, paragraph Ad sic dictam missam praesanctificatorum.

evidence.locus: Printed 14 / PDF 19, Ad sic dictam missam praesanctificatorum
evidence.claim: Names the 1843 editor’s compilation and says a manuscript Basil-labelled form replaces it.
Explicit original revision description identifies the 1843 predecessor and bounded changes.

transitions.limitations: The original 1843 book is acquired and its Presanctified opening inspected; the prayer-body changes here still depend on the 1922 editor’s description. Native repertoire-label comparison is recorded separately. Additional 1922 changes are not all tied to exact 1843 leaves. The 1881 minister book remains complementary, not the predecessor of the 1922 altar book.

gaps.missing: No identified sequence of Catholic received manuscript exemplars. Project entries for Add. 14523, ff. 1–7 (eighth/ninth century), and Add. 14690 (main copy 1182) are shared witnesses, not Catholic stages. Rahmani 1922 cites British Museum and patriarchal-library manuscripts; his page 12 footnote needs disambiguation; Add. 17128 is explicitly cited on pages 13–14.
gaps.next_source: William Wright, Catalogue of Syriac Manuscripts in the British Museum I (1870), entries Add. 14523, Add. 14690 and Add. 17128; current British Library images; Sharfeh patriarchal manuscript catalogue; Rahmani 1922, pages 12–14.
gaps.consequence: Cannot draw common ancestry as Catholic reception or assign one copy date across composite manuscript layers.

gaps.missing: Full before/after collation of the 1843 and 1922 native prayer bodies. The original 1843 full PDF, title, patriarchal attestation and imprimaturs are now acquired and checked.
gaps.next_source: Retained edition.syriac-catholic-church.missale-syriacum.1843-rome-propaganda; compare native entrance prayers and Presanctified form with held Sharfeh 1922.
gaps.consequence: Established primary-described revision remains source-described, not an actual before/after Syriac comparison.

gaps.missing: The 1868 first edition, undated patriarch-approved reprint and 1905 Sharfeh complete diaconicon have not been inspected.
gaps.next_source: Ziadé 1941, column 3026; Mosul Service de la messe privée, 1868; Sharfeh diaconicon, 1905; compare held 1881 ordinary and contents.
gaps.consequence: No additional auxiliary book stages or evolution edges created from bibliographical dates alone.

gaps.next_source: Syriac Catholic Patriarchate and Sharfeh seminary press catalogues; Edmund Rücker, “Das neue syrische Missale”, Jahrbuch für Liturgiewissenschaft 4 (1924), 187–192, for immediate reception.

gaps.next_source: 1934 Pampakuda copy via Malankara Catholic archives, SEERI or Malankara Library; Tisserant, DTC column 3160; Codrington, Eastern Churches Quarterly 1, no. 3 (July 1936), page 98.

A pastoral letter dated 15 February 2007 reports an already published renewed Holy Qurbono order with Qyomto and Sleebo prayers, available at eparchial centres; the later October release report may concern another publication state.

Compare the October 2007 release in Synodal Acts 3.2, p 25 and concelebration decision p 40. English/Malayalam synod years conflict (2005/2006).
